metadata.case_name: LAM SHU TAK THOMAS v. LING SHUM HA AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.education_level: university degree with a diploma of education

injuries.description: His aortic arch was ruptured or torn.
source: His aortic arch was ruptured or torn.

injuries.description: His left carotid artery was avulsed or completely ripped off.
source: His left carotid artery was avulsed or completely ripped off.

injuries.description: His left subclavian artery was thrombosed or blocked.
source: His left subclavian artery was thrombosed or blocked.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of innominate or subclavian artery

injuries.description: The plaintiff was injured and received extensive vascular and muscular damage.
source: The plaintiff was injured and received extensive vascular and muscular damage.

injuries.description: The severance of the axillary nerve leading to partial paralysis of the deltoid muscle (70% nerve damage) affecting the right shoulder.
source: but the most damaging injury to the right shoulder is the severance of the axillary nerve leading to partial paralysis of the the deltoid muscle.

injuries.description: Fracture dislocation of the elbow with imperfect union resulting in limited flexion.
source: Because of the fracture dislocation of the elbow in the accident, he can only bend it 110o instead of 160o.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the elbow or forearm

injuries.description: Jaw bone fractured and loss of five teeth.
source: The plaintiff lost five teeth and had his jaw bone fractured in the accident.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of alveolar margin of mandible

injuries.description: Divers surgical scars on the face causing disfigurement principally due to the right nostril and upper lip wounds.
source: His two major operations left him with divers surgical scars. The scars on his face brought him disfigurement principally due to the right nostril and upper lip wounds.

injuries.description: Evidence of brain damage: a hypodense area over the left parietal region on C.A.T. scan.
source: Dr. Cheung was positive that a hypodense area over the left parietal region measured 3 c.m. by 8 m.m. and shown in one slide of a Computerized Axle Tomogram called, for short, "C.A.T. Scan" was evidence of brain damage.

manifestations.description: Dizzy spells / vertigo and fainting spells
Subclavian steal syndrome (diminution of blood supply to the brain)
Atrophy/wasting of the deltoid muscle (70% nerve damage)
Limited range of movement of right arm (cannot raise straight up; can raise almost to shoulder level; limited external and internal rotation)
Reduced elbow flexion (can only bend to 110 degrees)
Loss of some grip in right hand; right palm trembles; difficulty holding a pen or a pair of chopsticks

treatments_received: First operation by Dr. Nandi on the 7th August 1979: the ruptured aortic arch was repaired by a dacron patch.
Aortogram confirming blockage of left subclavian artery (diagnostic).
Second major operation on the 10th April, 1980 by Dr. Dandi: a dacron bypass was constructed for this subclavian artery.
Readmitted to the Grantham Hospital on the 6th August, 1980 for treatment of dizzy spells; given a cervical collar for a fortnight in hospital and wore it for a further two weeks thereafter.
Readmitted in February 1981 for two fainting spells and was admitted to hospital.
treatments_future: Limited plastic surgery advised by Dr. Nicholson to the right nostril area and the right knee (approximately $8,200).

losses.description: Partial paralysis of the deltoid muscle (70% nerve damage) and persistent right arm impairment including atrophy, pain and reduced range of movement.
Surgical scars on his face causing disfigurement principally due to the right nostril and upper lip wounds.

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Difficulty holding a pen or a pair of chopsticks; reduced grip in right hand.
No longer managerial material; can only cope with junior clerical work; substantial loss of future earning capacity and prospects.
An assessed 25% loss of expectation of life.
